brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A downy large-leaf Yunnan tea listed as a specialty of Yingjiang county, though accounts also place it in Yangta village, Jinggu. Despite the name, today it is made as a baked green tea.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: A local story credits a trader named Chen Liujiu with smuggling seeds home to Yangta in a bamboo carrying pole around 1840. In the Qing period it was tied with red silk into grain-ear bundles and sent as tribute under the name Bai Long Xu. It was named a provincial famous tea in 1981.
processing: Formerly fixed by hand, rolled, half sun-dried, rolled again and sun-dried. Now fixed, rolled and baked.
harvest_season: Around Qingming, one bud with two or three opening leaves.
appearance_dry: Long, stout strands with glinting silver down.
appearance_wet: Leaves hang in the glass like magnolia petals.
taste_profile: Rich, fresh aroma with a mellow body and returning sweetness; older accounts note an olive-like fragrance.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
